title: Proximity-based request-steering explainer and localized onboarding screens
creator: Aria Patel
description: Create a compact explainer and a set of localized onboarding screens that show how Redwood routes requests based on geographic proximity, capacity awareness, and configured routing policies. Deliverables: 1) One-page explainer diagram that layers the routing decision process (client region detection, regional pool selection, capacity fallback, model-variant downgrade). 2) Three onboarding screens for the Quickstart flow (initial map view, interactive region selector, and failure/fallback state). 3) Exported assets (SVGs and PNGs) and developer-ready specs for implementation in the Console. Focus is on clarity for engineers and product teams during first-run setup; avoid brand-heavy illustrations so assets can be reused in docs and emails.
acceptance_criteria: Explainer diagram communicates the 4-step routing decision path within 10 seconds to a reviewer; onboarding screens match Console typography and color tokens; interactive map states include: default region highlight, pinned-region, and automatic fallback overlay; exported assets include SVG + 2x PNG for each screen; dev spec includes exact spacing, colors (tokens), and microinteraction hints; UX approved by PM and Eng lead.
design_notes: Design uses a layered approach: top layer shows user request origin, middle layer shows policy/routing engine, bottom layer indicates target pool. Chose a semi-transparent 'ribbon' motif to convey routing corridors rather than heat blobs to avoid implying fixed latency values. Trade-offs: simplified corridor visuals instead of raw RTT numbers to reduce cognitive load during onboarding. Accessibility: ensure color contrast meets AA for primary corridor colors and provide text alternatives for map states. Interaction: map zoom should animate corridor width to suggest confidence, but keep animations subtle to avoid distraction on low-powered machines.
